# Next.js App Router — Dialog / Modal / Popup Pattern

## Component name conventions

| Suffix | Use for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `*Popup` | Lightweight overlays — pickers, selectors | `IconSelectPopup.tsx`, `TypeSelectPopup.tsx`, `CodeInputPopup.tsx` |
| `*Modal` | Fuller dialogs — notifications, detail views | `NotificationModal.tsx` |
| `*Dialog` | Reserved for system confirmation dialogs | (use Mantine's `modals.openConfirmModal()` instead) |

Convention: use **`Popup` for most custom overlays** and **`Modal` for content-heavy panels**. They both wrap Mantine's `Modal` component — the suffix communicates intent.

---

## Folder placement

| Scope | Location |
|---|---|
| Feature-scoped (used by one screen) | `app/(app)/{feature}/_components/XxxPopup.tsx` |
| Shared across features | `app/(core)/_components/XxxPopup.tsx` |

For detail/edit screens, `_components/` lives directly under `[id]/` so both `view/` and `edit/` siblings can import the popup:

```
app/(app)/resources/[id]/
├── page.tsx
├── _components/
│   └── IconSelectPopup.tsx   # shared by view/ and edit/
├── view/
└── edit/
```

---

## Standard Props shape

```tsx
type Props = {
  /** 開閉状態 */
  opened: boolean
  /** 閉じるコールバック */
  close: () => void
  /** 確定時のコールバック（オプション） */
  onConfirm?: (value: SomeType) => void
  /** 初期値 */
  initialValue?: SomeType
}
```

Rules:
- `opened` (boolean) + `close` (function) are the canonical pair — match Mantine's `useDisclosure` API
- Confirm-style popups take `onConfirm(value)`; the popup calls `close()` after invoking it
- Never internally manage `opened` — always control from the parent

---

## Full example — IconSelectPopup

```tsx
// app/(app)/resources/[id]/_components/IconSelectPopup.tsx
"use client"

import { Modal, Group, ActionIcon, ColorPicker, Stack } from "@mantine/core"
import { useState } from "react"
import { IconCheck } from "@tabler/icons-react"

type Props = {
  opened: boolean
  close: () => void
  setIcon: (iconId: number) => void
  setColor: (color: string) => void
  currentIconId: number
  currentColor: string
}

/** アイコン選択ポップアップ */
export const IconSelectPopup = ({ opened, close, setIcon, setColor, currentIconId, currentColor }: Props) => {
  const [draftIcon, setDraftIcon] = useState(currentIconId)
  const [draftColor, setDraftColor] = useState(currentColor)

  const handleConfirm = () => {
    setIcon(draftIcon)
    setColor(draftColor)
    close()
  }

  return (
    <Modal opened={opened} onClose={close} title="アイコン選択" centered>
      <Stack gap="md">
        {/* アイコン一覧 */}
        <Group>
          {ICON_OPTIONS.map((icon) => (
            <ActionIcon
              key={icon.id}
              size="xl"
              variant={draftIcon === icon.id ? "filled" : "default"}
              onClick={() => setDraftIcon(icon.id)}
            >
              {icon.element}
            </ActionIcon>
          ))}
        </Group>

        {/* カラー選択 */}
        <ColorPicker value={draftColor} onChange={setDraftColor} />

        {/* 確定ボタン */}
        <Group justify="flex-end">
          <ActionIcon onClick={handleConfirm}><IconCheck /></ActionIcon>
        </Group>
      </Stack>
    </Modal>
  )
}
```

---

## Parent usage

### Open/close via `useDisclosure`

```tsx
// app/(app)/resources/[id]/edit/ResourceEditScreen.tsx
"use client"

import { useDisclosure } from "@mantine/hooks"
import { IconSelectPopup } from "../_components/IconSelectPopup"

const ResourceEditScreen = () => {
  const [iconPopupOpened, { open: openIconPopup, close: closeIconPopup }] = useDisclosure(false)
  const { watch, setValue } = useResourceForm({ resourceId })

  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={openIconPopup}>アイコンを選択</Button>

      <IconSelectPopup
        opened={iconPopupOpened}
        close={closeIconPopup}
        currentIconId={watch().iconId}
        currentColor={watch().iconColor}
        setIcon={(id) => setValue("iconId", id)}
        setColor={(color) => setValue("iconColor", color)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Multiple popups on one screen

```tsx
const [iconOpen,  { open: openIcon,  close: closeIcon  }] = useDisclosure(false)
const [memberOpen,{ open: openMember,close: closeMember}] = useDisclosure(false)
const [colorOpen, { open: openColor, close: closeColor }] = useDisclosure(false)
```

Each popup gets its own `useDisclosure` — never share state between unrelated popups.

---

## Modal API

Wrap Mantine's `<Modal>`:

```tsx
<Modal
  opened={opened}
  onClose={close}
  title="アイコン選択"
  centered
  size="md"             // xs | sm | md | lg | xl | full
  overlayProps={{ backgroundOpacity: 0.55, blur: 3 }}
  withCloseButton={true}
  closeOnClickOutside={true}
  closeOnEscape={true}
>
  {/* content */}
</Modal>
```

| Prop | When to override |
|---|---|
| `centered` | Default. Set `position={{ top: 100 }}` for off-center if needed. |
| `size` | `md` is default; use `lg`/`xl` only when content needs it. |
| `closeOnClickOutside` | Set to `false` for destructive confirmation dialogs. |
| `closeOnEscape` | Set to `false` if Escape conflicts with inner shortcuts. |
| `withCloseButton` | Set to `false` only when an explicit confirm/cancel button pair is the only exit. |

---

## Confirm dialog — use `modals.openConfirmModal()`

For simple yes/no prompts, do not write a custom Modal. Use Mantine's imperative API:

```tsx
import { modals } from "@mantine/modals"
import { Text } from "@mantine/core"

const askDelete = () => {
  modals.openConfirmModal({
    title: "削除確認",
    centered: true,
    children: (
      <Text size="sm">本当に削除してよろしいですか？この操作は取り消せません。</Text>
    ),
    labels: { confirm: "削除する", cancel: "キャンセル" },
    confirmProps: { color: "red" },
    onConfirm: () => handleDelete(),
  })
}
```

`ModalsProvider` is already configured in `app/(core)/_components/providers.tsx`.

> When confirmation is part of a mutation hook (`useDeleteXxx`), prefer `window.confirm()` for synchronous flow. Use `modals.openConfirmModal()` when richer markup or styling is needed.

---

## Draft state vs immediate commit

Two ways to handle popup input:

### A. Draft state — confirm to commit

The popup tracks a local `draft` and only commits on "Confirm":

```tsx
const [draft, setDraft] = useState(initialValue)
const handleConfirm = () => {
  onConfirm(draft)
  close()
}
```

Use this when:
- The choice is non-trivial (icon + color picker, complex form)
- Cancel should revert without side effects
- The selection has multiple sub-values

### B. Immediate commit — close to confirm

Each interaction immediately propagates to the parent; closing is the confirmation:

```tsx
<Select
  value={current}
  onChange={(v) => setValue("category", v)}  // commits immediately
/>
```

Use this when:
- The choice is a single tap (radio buttons, simple list)
- Parent state should reflect changes in real time

---

## Scroll lock and stacking

Mantine's Modal automatically:
- Locks body scroll while open
- Stacks correctly when multiple modals are open
- Returns focus to the trigger on close

Do not manually manage `overflow: hidden` on `body` or implement custom focus traps.

---

## Animation

Mantine includes built-in slide/fade transitions. Override with `transitionProps` if needed:

```tsx
<Modal transitionProps={{ transition: "slide-up", duration: 200 }}>
```

---

## When NOT to use a modal

Reach for a modal only when the interaction must:
1. Block all other interactions on the page
2. Capture focus until completed
3. Be dismissed explicitly (not by scrolling away)

Otherwise, prefer:
- **Drawer** (Mantine `Drawer`) — side panel, less intrusive
- **Popover** (Mantine `Popover`) — anchored to a trigger element
- **Inline expansion** — accordion or expanding card section
- **Separate route** — for content-heavy or shareable views (e.g. navigate to `RESOURCE_URL.view(id)` instead of opening a modal)

---

## Constraints

- `opened: boolean` + `close: () => void` is the canonical prop pair
- Use `useDisclosure()` for state — never reinvent open/close with `useState`
- Multiple popups on one screen get separate `useDisclosure` instances
- Confirm-style popups: draft state inside, commit via `onConfirm`
- Use Mantine's `<Modal>` — do not write a custom backdrop/portal
- For yes/no prompts, use `modals.openConfirmModal()`; for in-mutation prompts, use `window.confirm()` for synchronous flow
- Never manage `body` overflow manually
- Popups shared between `view/` and `edit/` belong in `[id]/_components/`, not inside the view/edit folders
